# Lenses

Lenses contains declared modes of reading through which one object discloses different operations. The register currently holds the twelve MEF lens records, declared from the internal-corpus house [Taylor — MEF Twelve Lenses Reference (2026)](../sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-mef-twelve-lenses/taylor-2026-mef-twelve-lenses.md) (`source_id: taylor-2026-mef-twelve-lenses`). Each record carries that house's recovered compilation entry for its lens — anchor, tonic and ground-pair; the six-sublens internal rotation; the 8-fold and diatonic derivation at its index; and its declared twin, complement and Möbius relations — and invents no content. The compilation is a derived synthesis reference: its historical attributions keep their own public-source obligations, and its musical selection keeps a separate derivational debt.

MEF lenses refract a canonical object; they do not replace it with a private summary. A lens is a tonic that rotates the full `6+6` — the Name hexad and the Power hexad — onto its ground: same-index Day/Night twins share one rotated field read from opposite faces, and lens-modulation is epistemic-mode-modulation, not a change of private vocabulary. Multiple lenses can converge, diverge or qualify one another while the source, argument or scene retains its own identity. A lens enters a public page only when it changes what can be seen or tested there.

The pre-lens potential (`6² × 2 = 72`), the three concomitant grains (`6+6`, the 8-fold, the 7-fold diatonic) and the master rotation tables remain with the house and its recovered compilation; this index does not duplicate them. The register's earlier two developed readings — Baudrillard's simulation lens and Foucault's knowledge/power lens — were homed on 2026-09-25 into their source houses ([Baudrillard — Symbolic Exchange and Death (1976)](../sources/media-technology-philosophy/baudrillard/baudrillard-1976-symbolic-exchange-death/baudrillard-1976-symbolic-exchange-death.md#baudrillard-lens-reading) and [Foucault — The History of Sexuality, Volume 1 (1976)](../sources/phenomenology-continental-philosophy/foucault/foucault-1976-history-sexuality-v1/foucault-1976-history-sexuality-v1.md#foucault-lens-reading)), where they now stand as declared lens readings rather than lens records.
